name: Do I need to replace my bathroom flooring when getting a new vanity?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace my bathroom flooring when getting a new vanity?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do not always need new flooring, but the new vanity must have a footprint equal to or larger than the previous cabinet to conceal unfinished subfloor areas. Builders often tile around vanities rather than beneath them. If your new unit is narrower, shallower, or a wall-hung floating design, bare subfloor, mismatched tile edges, or raw baseboards will be exposed. In those situations, you must either patch the flooring with matching materials, install a vanity with an identical footprint, or retile the bathroom floor before the new unit is secured.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not if the new vanity footprint covers the old one completely. If the new cabinet is smaller or wall-mounted, you will need to patch or replace the exposed floor.
